title: Establishment and Fractionation of Metastatic Axillary Lymph Node Cell Suspension
author: Ivanović, Dedović-Tanić, et al.

steps.title: Thaw and weigh tissue
steps.instruction: Quickly thaw frozen axillary lymph node (ALN) tissue on ice, measure its weight, and place it in a small glass Petri dish.

steps.title: Chop tissue and add PBS
steps.instruction: Using a scalpel, finely chop the weighed ALN tissue, then add 4 × 1 mL of phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS) to the pieces.

steps.title: Filter through 100 µm sieve
steps.instruction: Transfer the PBS‑suspended tissue onto an INOX 18/10 sieve (mesh 100 × 100 µm, net diameter ≈ 20 mm) placed above a fresh Petri dish; pulverize the tissue on the sieve surface with a rubber piston to separate fat and connective tissue, allowing intact cells to pass through the mesh into the dish.

steps.title: Centrifuge cell suspension
steps.instruction: Collect the filtrate (cell suspension) into an Eppendorf tube and centrifuge at 850 g for 15 min at 4 °C; decant the supernatant and estimate the packed cell‑pellet volume (Vpack).

steps.title: Dilute pellet in hypotonic buffer
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in ice‑cold hypotonic lysis buffer at a volume of 5 × Vpack and keep on ice.

steps.title: Count viable cells
steps.instruction: Take a 50 µL aliquot of the pooled cell pellet, mix with Trypan blue, and count viable cells using a Neubauer hemocytometer.

steps.title: Fractionate into cytosolic and nuclear extracts
steps.instruction: Perform the following sequential operations on the hypotonic‑lysed cell suspension to obtain separate cytosolic and nuclear fractions.

substeps.instruction: 1. Incubate the lysate on ice for 15 min to allow cell swelling.
2. Centrifuge at 850 g for 15 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.
3. Resuspend the resulting pellet (from all tubes) again in 5 × Vpack of ice‑cold hypotonic lysis buffer, pool into one tube, and centrifuge at 850 g for 15 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.
4. Resuspend the pellet in 2 × Vpack of ice‑cold hypotonic lysis buffer and homogenize by drawing the suspension into a syringe and ejecting it through a 27‑gauge needle.
5. Centrifuge the homogenate at 8,000 g for 20 min at 4 °C; collect the supernatant (cytosolic extract) and set aside 50 µL for total cytosolic protein measurement.
6. Aliquot the remaining cytosolic extract, snap‑freeze in liquid nitrogen, and store at –70 °C (shelf life ≤ 4 months) for TGFβ1 ELISA.
7. Resuspend the resulting nuclear pellet on ice in nuclear extraction buffer at a volume of 1 × Vpack.
8. Lyse nuclei by drawing the suspension into a syringe and ejecting it through a 27‑gauge needle; add 1 % Igepal CA‑630 if needed.
9. Gently agitate the lysate for 30 min on ice, then centrifuge at 18,000 g for 10 min at 4 °C.
10. Collect the supernatant (nuclear extract) and take an aliquot for total nuclear protein determination.
11. Aliquot the remaining nuclear extract, snap‑freeze in liquid nitrogen, and store at –70 °C for cFOS analysis.
